question: The simple interest on a principal amount (in ₹) is ₹714 for a period of 3 years at the rate of 7% per annum. The principal amount (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total simple interest percentage = Rate × Time = 7% × 3 = 21%

Given that 21% of the principal = ₹714

⇒ 1% of principal = 714 ÷ 21 = 34

⇒ 100% (Principal) = 34 × 100 = 3400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹714

Rate of Interest (R) = 7% per annum

Time Period (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 Year 0

 P = ?
 7%

 Total SI = ₹714 (21%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 714 = (P × 7 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 714 = (P × 21) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (714 × 100) ÷ 21

⇒ P = 34 × 100

⇒ P = 3400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after a given time period is the sum of the principal and the earned interest: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest percentage is calculated only on the original principal amount. In Compound Interest, the interest is calculated on both the principal and the previously accumulated interest.

Rule of 72

A quick mathematical trick used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given fixed annual interest rate: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate.
